text:
Alex K: heads-up — seeing a small but reproducible set of requests in canary that get stale prefix reads after a handoff. i can repro locally with the handoff test harness. logs below:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z INFO handoff: initiator=shard-7 target=shard-12 prefix=tenant/42 epoch=102
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z INFO apply: prefix=tenant/42 read_at_epoch=101 served_from_cache=true
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z WARN consistency: mismatch detected read_epoch=101 owner_epoch=102
```
nothing catastrophic, but causes client-visible stale reads for ~200ms until a subsequent write clears it. curious if this is an ordering gap between lease revoke and last-applied update. pinging eng-runtime to sanity-check ideas. :thinking:
text_followups: Maria D: ack. saw similar spikes in infra canary last week though we chalked them up to head-of-line with prefetch. can you paste the minimal repro?

Alex K: repro is a tiny harness: allocate prefix on node A -> write -> trigger handoff -> immediately read prefetched key on node B. sometimes node B serves cached KV with previous epoch. i'll drop the harness link in the ticket.

Samir R: quick thought — do we have a guaranteed ordering that the handoff marker is visible to readers before we flip the lease? my mental model was: write last_applied -> write handoff marker -> revoke lease. if revoke happens before marker visible, readers on new owner may not see last_applied.

Lee P: +1. in practice the seq path is: apply snapshot -> grant ownership token -> async notify observers. there is a visibility window while KV cache warmup finishes. that window could overlap with reads if we advertise ownership early.

Alex K: exact. the log shows owner_epoch=102 but read_at_epoch=101. looks like read path used cached entry that didn't have the final marker. so we need either stronger handshake or a fast invalidation path.

Maria D: short-term mitigation idea: when handoff completes, publish a small invalidation TTL for that prefix to the global invalidation channel so other nodes drop cached entries immediately. cheap and surgical.

Samir R: that helps but relies on best-effort pubsub; if invalidation is lost we still have stale reads. we could also tag cache entries with epoch and make read path check owner epoch from a compact map before serving. cheap check if epoch mismatch -> force forward-read from store.

Lee P: epoch-check on read is nice: logic: cached_entry.epoch >= owner_map[prefix] ? serve : fetch-from-store. owner_map is small (per-shard prefix table) and kept in memory. adds one memory lookup and prevents stale-serving.

Alex K: performance impact should be minimal for most reads but we must avoid hot-looping on owner_map fetch under high QPS. maybe use a fast-read snapshot (RCU-like) and only do store fetch on mismatch.

Maria D: ops question: what about eviction interplay? if we aggressively invalidate, we'll push lots of rehydrates and risk cascading cold starts. need a backoff: invalidate only if epoch delta > 0 or if writes occurred within last X ms.

Samir R: agreed. policy: if new_owner_epoch > cached_epoch then if (now - last_write_ts < 500ms) do full eviction-and-prefill, else lazy-serve-stale-with-warning. that reduces churn for truly cold prefixes.

Lee P: for correctness, lazy-stale is risky for customers expecting linearizable semantics. maybe we should define SLAs: hosted API default is eventual-consistency with a short staleness window, but enterprise private can opt into stronger "handoff-atomic" mode that enforces flushes at handoff time.

Alex K: that's a product-level decision — we can implement both modes. for now, i propose two engineering tracks: 1) short-term: read-epoch-check + best-effort invalidation channel + canary rollout. 2) long-term: handshake refactor so handoff isn't advertised until kv snapshot and last_applied are both visible (atomic transfer).
Maria D: +1. short-term rollout plan: implement epoch-check in read path behind a runtime flag, enable on canary for 48h, watch metrics: stale-read-rate, rehydrate QPS, latency p99. create dashboard.
Samir R: i'll take the read-path PR and add unit tests covering epoch mismatch, lost invalidation, and perf microbench. i'll also add a metric `evict.invalidation_fallbacks`.

Lee P: I'll wire up the invalidation publish/subscribe endpoint to the handoff flow and add a Config knob to tune the 500ms window Maria suggested. also will add a kill-switch to revert if we see rehydrate storms.

Alex K: action items: Samir -> PR for epoch-check + tests, Lee -> invalidation channel + knob, Maria -> dashboard and canary plan, Alex -> open a short RFC describing the handshake refactor and backward-compat constraints. timeline: land short-term mitigations this sprint (1w), canary 48h, then decide if we need immediate rollback.
Maria D: also adding customer-impact check: create query to find tenants that hit >0 stale reads in last 7d, flag and notify customer-success if high. want to be proactive.
Samir R: small nit: make sure cache-entry structure versioned so we can roll forward/back without mixed-schema. i can add a version header in the cached blob.
Lee P: noted. i'll ensure invalidation messages include prefix, new_epoch, and an opaque nonce for debugging. ops-bot will emit an alert when invalidation-fallbacks > 10/min in canary.
evict-bot: NOTICE: canary invalidation channel subscription established on 3 nodes. monitoring hook installed.
Alex K: great. if no objections i'll open the RFC draft tonight and assign owners. thanks all — we should be able to close the immediate customer risk without a heavy refactor.
Maria D: fine by me. :thumbsup:
Samir R: ok will start on test harness integration today.
Lee P: merging infra pieces tomorrow. i'll post a short followup when canary is live.
Alex K: closing the loop here when canary hits 48h or we hit any regression. thanks
